articles.text:
ODAIA Raises Series C to Scale Predictive Commercial Intelligence for Pharma
News provided by
ODAIA
Nov 17, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Returning investors and strategic investor PHM back
ODAIA's next stage of growth
BOSTON , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ODAIA , an AI company delivering predictive commercial intelligence for pharma, today announced it has closed a US$15 million Series C financing led by Monograph Capital and anchored by strategic investor PHM , the leading health media agency in the U.S., part of Publicis Groupe. Investors from ODAIA's earlier rounds are also returning: BDC Capital , Flint Capital , Innospark Ventures , and Graphite Ventures from its Series A and Threshold Ventures and Wittington Ventures from its Series B. ODAIA will use the capital to grow within the enterprise pharma accounts it already serves and continue innovating its commercial intelligence platform.
Leading biopharmaceutical companies use ODAIA for commercial intelligence and workflow automations for field and marketing teams across many therapeutic areas. ODAIA predicts patient journeys, uncovers missed Rx opportunities, determines which healthcare professionals (HCPs) to prioritize through which channels, and keeps sales and marketing working from one brand strategy.
"Pharma has proven that AI works in commercial. The hard part now is scaling it," said Philip Poulidis , CEO and co-founder of ODAIA. "Most companies can show results on one brand, and every new brand or therapeutic area still costs another team and another build. ODAIA started by helping field teams decide where to focus. Today our platform is the commercial intelligence infrastructure that scales what's working across brand, marketing, and field teams, and across a company's whole portfolio. This round lets us go deeper with the enterprise customers we already serve and, with PHM, bring that infrastructure to more of the industry, faster."
"We have watched the ODAIA team turn predictive AI into decisions that pharma brand and field teams act on every day," said Charles Conn , co-founder and partner at Monograph Capital, which co-led ODAIA's Series B and led this round. "The ODAIA team has a track record of helping large and specialty pharma brands reach the physicians whose patients need their therapies most."
One strategy for brand, field, and marketing
Inside most pharma companies, data sits in many systems owned by separate teams, so brand, marketing, and field each work from a different picture of the same physician. Patients get missed, field and digital effort lands in the wrong places, and nobody can say with confidence what is influencing HCP decisions. ODAIA's commercial intelligence platform provides the foundation underneath. It brings disparate data, field sales activity, and digital engagement into one view of each HCP that brand, marketing, and field teams all work from.
Brand teams codify their strategy once in Brand Strategy Studio , and ODAIA's decision engines turn it into HCP-level choices about who to reach, through which channel, when, and with what message. Extending to a new brand or therapeutic area is a matter of configuration. The platform identifies physicians whose patients are likely to need a therapy, often months before a diagnosis shows up in the data. AI video production startup Lemonpeel raises $1 Mn in pre-seed round led by Shastra VC
AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Sta
Gyan Vardhan
17 Nov 2026
14:09
IST
Follow Us
New Update
AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Startups and Claude Startup programmes.
The proceeds will be utilized to develop multi-agent platforms for video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery, marketing and go-to-market capabilities to reach more enterprise creative teams, and build intellectual property around faces and creative workflows, Lemonpeel said in a press release.
Co-founded in Sep. last year by Hardik Goyal, Riddhiman Pal and Abhinav Nikam, Lemonpeel builds AI video production infrastructure for enterprise creative teams that brings together video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery through specialised agents and a model-agnostic engine. It works with customers in India and the UAE.
The Mumbai-based startup combines specialised AI agents with a model-agnostic engine that routes tasks across more than 300 models, including Veo, Kling and Seedance. A quality control layer helps maintain consistency in characters, logos and products.
The platform supports translation and subtitles in more than 100 languages and can also be used from inside AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The company is turning the production steps its team currently handles into product capabilities.
Lemonpeel is focused on media execution end-to-end: editing, maintaining visual consistency and preparing content for approval at scale. This is particularly relevant to films and campaigns that need multiple regional language versions and formats. The company plans to expand into MENA, US and Canada.
It competes with the other players in this space such as Runway, Google Flow, Higgsfield, Magnific, Flora, Weavy, and Invideo.
Startups in this space are developing AI-led platforms that automate video production workflows, generate multilingual and personalised videos, enable automated editing, and ensure quality and consistency before content is delivered across digital channels.
Meanwhile, Clueso raised $10 million in a Series A round in Oct. this year, led by Dharana Capital, to strengthen its AI agents and automate enterprise video creation and editing workflows.
TrueFan AI also secured $10 million in Series A funding in June this year, led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners, to scale its enterprise video-generation infrastructure. Other emerging players include CRAON, which raised pre-seed funding in May 2026 to develop its prompt-led AI video editing platform.

Hatz AI raises $24Mn Series A to sell AI through MSPs
Danica Macayan
Posted on November 17, 2026 2 min read
Copied URL
Key facts
Hatz AI raised $24 million in Series A funding.
Josh Schertzer of Nadia Partners led the deal.
Hatz’s active MSP partner count tripled year over year.
Hatz grew from 14 to nearly 60 employees.
Source: Hatz AI
NEW YORK, UNITED STATES — Hatz AI, which sells its artificial intelligence (AI) platform to small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) only through managed service providers (MSPs), has raised $24 million in Series A funding. Nadia Partners, Vestigo Ventures and The Private Shares Fund backed the round.
Josh Schertzer, a partner at Nadia Partners and former chief technology officer at Blackstone, led the deal.
AI sold under the MSP’s brand
Hatz announced the funding in a press release on Nov. 12.
Its platform gives MSPs multi-tenant AI governance, custom workflows and automated routing across leading foundation models. MSPs can then package and deliver AI-as-a-Service under their own brand.
Hatz said it has no competing direct-to-enterprise sales and has issued more than 15,000 AI certifications to builders globally.
The investment will help it scale a partner network that it said spans thousands of MSPs in all 50 U.S. states, nine Canadian provinces and nine countries.
Partners triple, staff quadruple
Hatz said its active MSP partner count tripled year over year, while revenue grew even faster. It expanded its workforce from 14 to nearly 60 employees.
The company is expanding in Flatiron, New York City, and scaling its forward deployed engineer team to work alongside partners. It is also growing its AI research and AI optimization teams.
“Small businesses represent the backbone of the global economy, and the managed service providers they already rely on are exactly the people to lead this transformation,” said Jimmy Hatzell, chief executive and co-founder of Hatz AI.
“By giving MSPs full control over governance, spend, and deployment, we’re making it possible for every small business to become AI native,” Hatzell said.
What the money funds
The new capital will deepen platform capabilities, including Hatz’s auto-model routing engine, benchmarks and internal software factory infrastructure. Hatz will also keep recruiting engineers for its forward deployed engineering and AI research units.
“By focusing exclusively on powering MSPs rather than trying to sell directly to end-users, Hatz has built a true dominance in channel-delivered AI,” Schertzer said.
What it means for buyers
Investors are backing a model in which smaller companies get AI from the IT provider they already pay, rather than from the model makers directly. For businesses that buy managed services or information technology outsourcing (ITO) , that puts AI governance and spending decisions into an existing contract.

AI infra startup JohnAIC raises $1.9 Mn in pre-seed round
Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.
Shashank Pathak
17 Nov 2026
09:38
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.
The proceeds will be used to expand its manufacturing, configuration and supply capabilities for AI servers. It aims to scale production capacity to up to 100 AI servers per month.
Founded by Sasank Chilamkurthy, JohnAIC builds on-premise AI infrastructure combining GPU servers, inference software, optimised open-source models and local data management. Its integrated systems are designed to help enterprises deploy AI within their own environments while retaining control over computing resources, models and data.
The startup serves public sector organisations and large enterprises, including banks, healthcare companies and public sector undertakings (PSUs). For BFSI institutions, its systems enable AI deployment behind organisational firewalls and are designed to support DPDP and RBI requirements.
JohnAIC is also working with Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL). Its server infrastructure has been deployed for routine operational surveys, converting field data into real-time insights.
The company is expanding its factory and supply chain infrastructure to address demand from Indian enterprises building private AI environments and neocloud infrastructure.
